-health-check.name: -health-check
-health-check.description: Internal health check. Verifies workspace roots are accessible and ripgrep binary is available.

read.name: read
read.description: Read a text file with optional line-based pagination. Returns content formatted as "cat -n" (numbered lines) plus metadata (name, size, lineCount, kind). Use offset+limit for ranges or head/tail for the first/last N lines. Returns text content; binary files are rejected.

params.head: Return only the first N lines (overrides offset/limit)
params.tail: Return only the last N lines (overrides offset/limit)
params.includeRaw: If true, include raw content (without line numbers) in addition to formatted

read-batch.name: read-batch
read-batch.description: Read multiple text files in a single call. Returns an array with one entry per requested path (ok, content/error). Each file is read with the same default limits as `read`; pass perFileLimit to override. Failures on individual paths do not abort the batch.

write.name: write
write.description: Write content to a file, overwriting if it exists. Safety: an existing file must have been read first in this session (use `read` before overwriting). For new files, parent directories are created automatically. Use `edit` for in-place modifications and `append` for additions.

append.name: append
append.description: Append content to the end of a file. Creates the file (and parents) if it does not exist. Does NOT require a prior read (appends are non-destructive to existing content). For replacing content, use `write` (after `read`) or `edit`.

edit.name: edit
edit.description: Replace exact string occurrence(s) in a file. By default fails if `oldString` appears zero or multiple times — pass `replaceAll: true` to rewrite every match. The replacement is literal (no regex). Returns a unified diff of the change. For structured hunks use `patch`; for larger rewrites use `write`.

params.dryRun: Preview the change (returns diff without writing). Default false

patch.name: patch
patch.description: Apply a unified diff (patch format) to a file atomically. Useful for multi-hunk fixes where several edits must go together. Uses fuzzy matching (fuzzFactor 2) so minor context drift is tolerated. Returns whether all hunks applied. For single-point changes prefer `edit`.

params.dryRun: Preview the patch (returns diff without writing). Default false

list.name: list
list.description: List directory entries with metadata (name, type, size, mtime, kind). Optionally recursive via `depth`. Honors `ignore` patterns (glob-style) and `respectGitignore`. Paginates with `limit` + `cursor`. For a hierarchical view use `tree`; for pattern-based search use `glob`.

params.depth: Max recursion depth (0 = current dir only, default 0, max 20)
params.respectGitignore: If true, load .gitignore from the root and honor it. Requires the root to be a git repo (looks for .git/); standalone .gitignore files are not picked up

tree.name: tree
tree.description: Return a hierarchical JSON tree of a directory up to `depth` levels. Files have size and mtime; directories have children. Honors `ignore` patterns and `respectGitignore`. Capped by maxNodes to prevent runaway output. Use `list` for flat pagination or `glob` for pattern match.

stat.name: stat
stat.description: Return metadata for a single path: exists, type (file/directory/symlink), size, mtime, permissions. Does NOT read content. Prefer this over `read` when you only need to check existence or size.

glob.name: glob
glob.description: Find files matching a glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}"). Results sorted by mtime (most recently modified first). Honors `ignore` patterns and `respectGitignore`. Use `grep` for content search and `list` for flat directory listing.

grep.name: grep
grep.description: Search file contents for a regex pattern using ripgrep. `output_mode` controls the shape: "content" returns {file, line, match, context} objects; "files" returns one entry per matching file with matchCount; "count" returns only totals. Supports context lines (-B/-A), include glob, case insensitive, multiline. Shell-injection safe (args are not interpolated). For finding files by name use `glob`.

params.pattern: Regex pattern (Rust regex syntax via ripgrep)
params.path: Base directory or file (default: workspace root)
params.contextBefore: Lines of context before each match
params.contextAfter: Lines of context after each match
params.type: Pre-defined file type filter passed to ripgrep --type (e.g. js, py, rust, ts, go, md). Faster than `include` when targeting a known language
params.multiline: Allow pattern to match across newlines
params.respectGitignore: Honor .gitignore (default false). Requires the root to be a git repo (looks for .git/); standalone .gitignore files are not picked up
params.limit: Max matches or files to return (default 50, max 100)

delete.name: delete
delete.description: Delete a file or directory. Set `recursive: true` for non-empty directories. Idempotent: succeeds silently if the path does not exist (reports existed=false).

copy.name: copy
copy.description: Copy a file or directory. For directories set `recursive: true`. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite: true`. Parent directories of the destination are created automatically.

move.name: move
move.description: Move or rename a file or directory. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite: true`. Parent directories of the destination are created automatically.

mkdir.name: mkdir
mkdir.description: Create a directory. By default creates parent directories as needed (recursive). Idempotent: returns created=false if the directory already exists.

list-roots.name: list-roots
list-roots.description: List the workspace roots this MCA can access. Returns {count, roots[{path, exists, type}]}. Useful for auditing scope when a path is rejected by the sandbox.

read-media.name: read-media
read-media.description: Read a binary file (image, PDF, audio, archive, ...) and return base64 + detected MIME type via magic bytes. Returns {file, name, size, mimeType, base64, mtime}. Hard cap 10 MB; for text use `read`.

hash.name: hash
hash.description: Compute the cryptographic hash of a file (default sha256). Streams the file so it works on large files without loading them. Returns {file, name, algorithm, hash, size}. Useful for integrity checks and detecting changes between reads.

name: Filesystem (Admin)
description: Filesystem operations on host machine. Admin only. Same surface as mca.teros.filesystem but without workspace jail.

changelog.notes: Read, write, edit and patch files, search by name and content, and manage folders across the host machine
